question: Antral follicle count (AFC) on transvaginal ultrasound — the total number of 2–10 mm follicles in both ovaries on day 2–3 of the menstrual cycle — is a reliable marker of ovarian reserve that correlates with response to ovarian stimulation.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. AFC on day 2–3 TVS counts small antral follicles (2–10 mm) in both ovaries; the total correlates with the primordial follicle pool and is used alongside AMH to counsel couples on fertility prognosis.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. AFC is a well-validated, inexpensive marker of ovarian reserve. A low AFC (typically <5–7 total) predicts poor response to stimulation; a high AFC (>15–20) suggests risk of ovarian hyperstimulation. It is measured alongside AMH for reserve assessment.
